title: Cross Hedging, Minimum Variance, Beta Hedging & Metallgesellschaft

scenes.title: Cross Hedging: Beyond Identical Assets
scenes.purpose: Problem-first hook: why airlines and treasurers must hedge with non-identical contracts
takeaways: Firms often lack liquid futures for their exact commodity
Cross hedging uses correlated contracts on related assets
Optimal hedge sizing uses Minimum Variance Hedge Ratio

beats.speaker: novice

en.display: What happens when a company needs to hedge a commercial commodity, like jet fuel, that has no actively traded futures contract on any global exchange? Can hedging still work?

hi.display: अगर किसी कंपनी को जेट फ्यूल जैसी कमोडिटी को हेज करना हो जिसका कोई डायरेक्ट फ्यूचर्स कॉन्ट्रैक्ट एक्सचेंज पर ट्रेड ही नहीं होता, तो कंपनी क्या करेगी? क्या हेजिंग तब भी मुमकिन है?

beats.onScreenIntent: Opening dilemma question on cross hedging without direct contracts

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: In Part 1 of Chapter 3, we examined hedging when the underlying physical asset and the futures contract are identical. In those baseline cases, basis risk is modest. However, in the vast majority of real-world commercial operations, an exchange-traded futures contract matching the company's precise physical commodity simply does not exist.

hi.display: Part One mein humne dekha ki jab physical asset aur futures contract identical hon—jaise crude oil ko crude oil futures se hedge karna—toh basis risk kaafi manageable hota hai. Lekin real world commercial markets mein aksar ek critical problem aati hai: har physical commodity ka exact futures contract exchange par available nahi hota.

beats.onScreenIntent: The mentor defines the cross hedging imperative

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: This operational reality introduces Cross Hedging: the practice of hedging an exposure in one physical asset by taking a futures position in a different, but economically correlated, financial or commodity contract. A classic example is a commercial airline hedging millions of gallons of jet fuel using exchange-traded NYMEX heating oil futures.

hi.display: Is situation ko Cross Hedging kehte hain. Jab ek company kisi physical asset ki price volatility ko protect karne ke liye kisi doosre correlated asset ke futures contract ko use karti hai—jaise jet fuel price ko hedge karne ke liye heating oil futures use karna.

beats.onScreenIntent: Dangers of naive one-to-one hedging across differing volatilities

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: In this part, we examine the quantitative mechanics of cross hedging. The minimum variance hedge ratio means the ratio of futures to spot that minimizes price variance. Treasurers calculate this ratio to protect non-standard commercial assets.

hi.display: Is part mein hum cross hedging ke quantitative calculations master karenge. Minimum variance hedge ratio ka matlab hai futures aur spot ka wo ratio jo price variance ko minimize karta hai. Treasurers is formula se non-standard assets ko protect karte hain.

beats.onScreenIntent: Introduction of the Minimum Variance Hedge Ratio formula

scenes.title: Minimum Variance Hedge Ratio Formula
scenes.purpose: Mathematical breakdown of h* = rho * (sigma_S / sigma_F)
takeaways: Optimal hedge ratio minimizes variance of value changes
Formula: h-star equals rho times spot volatility over futures
Optimal contracts scale h-star by physical size over contract

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: By applying statistical optimization to minimize the variance of the hedged portfolio's value changes, John Hull derives the optimal Minimum Variance Hedge Ratio, denoted as h star. The formula states: h star equals rho multiplied by sigma S divided by sigma F.

hi.display: Statistical calculus apply karke John C. Hull ne Minimum Variance Hedge Ratio ka exact formula derive kiya hai: h star barabar rho guna sigma S divided by sigma F.

beats.onScreenIntent: Formula definition and mathematical derivation overview

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Let us define each variable carefully: rho is the linear correlation coefficient between the change in spot price delta S and the change in futures price delta F over the hedging horizon. Sigma S is the standard deviation of spot price changes, and sigma F is the standard deviation of futures price changes.

hi.display: Yahan rho spot price change delta S aur futures price change delta F ke beech ka statistical correlation coefficient hai. Sigma S spot price change ka standard deviation hai, aur sigma F futures price change ka standard deviation hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Explaining correlation rho and standard deviation ratio

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: What happens if futures volatility exceeds spot volatility? If the futures contract is more volatile than the underlying spot asset, each contract produces larger price swings. Consequently, fewer contracts are needed to offset spot movements, driving h star below one.

hi.display: Agar futures volatility spot se zyada ho toh kya hoga? Agar futures contract spot se zyada volatile ho, toh har contract zyada dollar movement produce karega. Isliye kam contracts ki zaroorat padegi aur h star ek se kam ho jayega.

beats.onScreenIntent: Regression interpretation: slope coefficient of OLS fit

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Once the optimal hedge ratio h star is determined, calculate the contracts. The required number N star equals h star multiplied by Q A divided by Q F. Here, Q A is the size of the physical asset, and Q F is the size of one futures contract.

hi.display: Optimal hedge ratio h star milne ke baad required contracts calculate kijiye. Total contracts N star barabar h star guna Q A divided by Q F hota hai. Yahan Q A physical exposure ka size hai, aur Q F ek futures contract ka size hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Hedge effectiveness formula R2 = rho squared

scenes.title: Worked Example: Airline Jet Fuel Cross Hedge
scenes.purpose: Numerical calculation of optimal contracts for airline hedging jet fuel with heating oil
takeaways: Airline hedges 2M gallons fuel with NYMEX heating oil
Optimal hedge ratio h-star is 0.78 from statistical data
Optimal contract count is 37.14 rounded to 37 contracts

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Let us walk through John Hull's renowned textbook example: a commercial airline must purchase two million gallons of jet fuel in one month. Because jet fuel futures do not trade with sufficient exchange liquidity, the airline's treasury desk decides to cross-hedge using NYMEX heating oil futures.

hi.display: Aaiye Hull ke famous airline jet fuel example ko step-by-step calculate karte hain. Ek airline company ko ek mahine baad twenty lakh gallons jet fuel purchase karna hai. Lekin jet fuel ka koi liquid futures contract exist nahi karta, isliye wo NYMEX heating oil futures select karti hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Givens setup: 2M gallons jet fuel, 42k contract size, volatilities

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Historical price changes yield the necessary statistical parameters. The standard deviation of jet fuel price changes is zero point zero two six three. Futures standard deviation is zero point zero three one three. Their statistical correlation rho is zero point nine two eight.

hi.display: Historical price changes se statistical parameters milte hain. Spot jet fuel volatility sigma S zero point zero two six three hai. Futures volatility sigma F zero point zero three one three hai. Dono ke beech correlation rho zero point nine two eight hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Step 1: Calculate h* = 0.7777

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Substituting these parameters into the formula gives h star equals 0.78. Because one NYMEX contract represents 42,000 gallons, the airline calculates 37.14 contracts. Rounding to the nearest whole contract gives 37 contracts.

hi.display: In values ko formula mein rakhne par h star 0.78 milta hai. Kyunki ek NYMEX contract 42,000 gallons ka hota hai, airline 37.14 contracts calculate karti hai. Round karke 37 contracts bante hain.

beats.onScreenIntent: Step 2: Calculate N* = 37.03, rounded to 37 contracts

data.title: Textbook Example: Airline Jet Fuel Cross Hedge
data.conclusion: The airline enters 37 long NYMEX heating oil futures contracts.

scenes.title: Settlement Friction: Forward vs Futures Tailing
scenes.purpose: Contrasting forward contract theoretical hedging with daily futures margin settlement
takeaways: Forwards settle at maturity while futures settle daily
Tailing the hedge neutralizes daily margin interest drag
Tailed contract sizing uses total dollar asset values

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: There is a subtle institutional distinction that quantitative asset managers must account for: daily settlement friction. In theoretical forward contracts, payoff occurs in a single lump sum at final maturity. But in futures markets, cash flows are realized and credited or debited every single afternoon through daily marking to market.

hi.display: Lekin theoretical hedge ratio mein ek subtle institutional detail abhi bhi baaki hai: daily settlement. Futures contracts mein profit aur loss har sham cash mein settle hota hai jise marking-to-market kehte hain.

beats.onScreenIntent: Forward contracts versus daily marking to market contrast

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Incorporating the interest rate discounting and reinvestment effects of these daily cash flows is known as Tailing the Hedge. When a hedge is tailed, the optimal hedge ratio is estimated using percentage returns on spot and futures rather than absolute dollar changes.

hi.display: Is daily cash flow ke interest aur reinvestment impact ko incorporate karne ki process ko Tailing the Hedge kaha jata hai. Isme raw price changes ki jagah percentage returns use kiye jate hain.

beats.onScreenIntent: Daily interest drag and reinvestment friction

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Under a tailed hedge framework, contract sizing uses total dollar values. The optimal number N star equals h star multiplied by portfolio value divided by futures value. This small adjustment neutralizes daily interest earned or paid on variation margin.

hi.display: Tailed hedge framework mein contract sizing total dollar value par hoti hai. Optimal contracts N star barabar h star guna portfolio value divided by futures value hota hai. Ye adjustment daily margin par milne ya dene wale interest ko neutralize karta hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Tailing formula resolution: N* = h* * (V_A / V_F)

left.heading: Untailed Forward Trap
points: Assumes single lump-sum cash settlement at final maturity
Ignores daily cash flow friction and interest discounting drag
Sizes contracts purely on physical volume without cash flow adjustment

right.heading: Tailed Futures Reality
points: Daily marking-to-market crediting or debiting margin cash flows
Estimates optimal hedge ratio using percentage returns rather than dollar changes
Sizes contracts using total dollar values: N-star equals h-star times portfolio value over futures value

verdict.text: Tailing neutralizes daily interest drag earned or paid on daily variation margin.

scenes.title: Stock Index Futures Hedging Formula
scenes.purpose: Mathematical derivation of portfolio beta hedging using index futures
takeaways: Stock index futures immunize portfolios without stock sales
Formula scales portfolio value by contract value and beta
Slashes transaction costs and avoids capital gains tax

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Now let us transition from physical commodities to equity portfolios. Suppose an institutional fund manager oversees a multi-million dollar equity portfolio. If the manager anticipates an impending macroeconomic downturn, how can they protect the portfolio against a severe market crash without liquidating their underlying stocks?

hi.display: Ab commodity markets se moving out karke hum equity markets mein enter karte hain. Agar ek fund manager ke paas multi-million dollar equity portfolio ho, toh wo broad market crash se kaise bachega?

beats.onScreenIntent: Introduction to equity index hedging and portfolio risk breakdown

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: John Hull explains that rather than selling individual shares, the fund manager hedges by shorting Stock Index Futures, such as the S&P 500 futures contract. The optimal number of contracts to completely immunize the portfolio is given by N star equals beta multiplied by V sub A divided by V sub F.

hi.display: John C. Hull explain karte hain ki portfolio ko hedge karne ke liye individual shares sell karne ki zaroorat nahi hoti. Manager stock index futures use karta hai. Optimal contracts ka formula hota hai: N star barabar beta guna V A divided by V F.

beats.onScreenIntent: Deconstructing systematic risk versus specific company alpha

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: In this formula, beta represents the portfolio's systematic sensitivity to the equity index. P is the total market value of the investment portfolio. A denotes the current market value of one index futures contract.

hi.display: Is formula mein beta stock portfolio ki market sensitivity ko represent karta hai. P investment portfolio ki total current market value hai. A ek stock index futures contract ki current market value hoti hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Formula N* = beta * (P / A) derivation

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Shorting index futures instead of selling individual equities delivers immense operational advantages. It slashes transaction costs and avoids disruptive tax consequences. Managers preserve their chosen stock selections.

hi.display: Direct shares bechne ke bajaye index futures short karna behtar hota hai. Ye transaction costs ko dramatically kam karta hai aur capital gains taxes bachata hai. Portfolio manager apne chosen stocks ko retain karta hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Contract value A = Index Price x Multiplier (e.g. S&P 500 x 250)

scenes.title: Causal Mechanism: Dynamic Beta Steering
scenes.purpose: Step-by-step mechanism for adjusting portfolio beta without liquidating underlying stocks
takeaways: Hedging allows tactical beta adjustment across cycles
Shorting index futures cuts portfolio beta to target level
Futures margin inflows cushion downside market plunges

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Hedging equity portfolios is not always about eliminating every drop of market risk. Market risk means market-wide volatility that affects all publicly traded stocks. Often, investment managers want to steer portfolio sensitivity dynamically.

hi.display: Equity portfolios ko hedge karne ka matlab hamesha market risk ko zero karna nahi hota. Market risk यानी market-wide volatility hoti hai jo sabhi stocks ko affect karti hai. Aksar fund managers portfolio sensitivity ko dynamically adjust karna chahte hain.

beats.onScreenIntent: The dilemma: why managers avoid selling high-conviction stocks

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: To reduce portfolio beta from beta to a lower target beta star, short index contracts. The required number equals beta minus beta star, multiplied by portfolio value divided by futures value. This defensiveness cushions potential market drops.

hi.display: Agar portfolio beta ko lower target beta star par lana ho, toh index futures short kijiye. Contracts ka number beta minus beta star, guna portfolio value divided by futures value hota hai. Ye strategy market decline ke dauran downside buffer deti hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: The formula N* = (beta - beta*) * (P / A) mechanism

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Conversely, to amplify exposure ahead of a rally, raise beta to a higher target beta star. The manager goes long futures contracts. The formula remains identical, generating a negative short position which represents buying futures.

hi.display: Iske opposite, market rally se pehle exposure badhane ke liye beta ko target beta star tak raise kijiye. Manager index futures buy karta hai. Formula bilkul same rehta hai aur negative sign futures buy karne ko indicate karta hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Synthetic beta adjustment advantages: zero tax, zero slippage

scenes.title: Individual Stocks & Long-Dated Hedging
scenes.purpose: Analyzing how index futures insulate individual high-conviction stock bets
takeaways: Stock risk splits into systematic risk and unique alpha
Alpha isolation strips market swings to isolate stock gains
Stack and roll renews short contracts for multi-year hedges

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: This powerful hedging framework applies directly to individual stock investments. Suppose an investor identifies a company with exceptional corporate earnings potential, but fears that broader macroeconomic headwinds could drag the entire stock market down.

hi.display: Ye same principle individual stocks par bhi apply hota hai. Agar aap kisi specific stock par highly bullish hain lekin overall market direction ke baare mein uncertain hain, toh aap stock ko buy karke uske beta ke proportionate index futures short kar sakte hain.

beats.onScreenIntent: Card 1: Risk decomposition into systematic and unsystematic

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: This strategy enables alpha isolation. Alpha isolation means removing broad market swings so returns depend entirely on superior stock picking. If an asset manager picks equities that outperform the index, shorting futures extracts excess alpha.

hi.display: Ye strategy alpha isolation enable karti hai. Alpha isolation ka matlab hai market swings ko remove karke returns ko pure stock picking par depend karwana. Agar manager ke shares index se behtar perform karte hain, toh short futures pure alpha deliver karta hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Card 2: Stripping broad market swings with index futures

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: What happens when corporate exposures extend over multiple years, but long-dated futures lack liquidity? Hedgers use stack and roll. Stack and roll means rolling front-month futures contracts forward periodically to maintain long-dated hedges.

hi.display: Jab corporate commitments kai saalon tak extend hoti hain aur long-dated futures liquid nahi hote, tab kya karein? Treasurers stack and roll deploy karte hain. Stack and roll ka matlab hai front-month contracts ko bar-bar roll karke long hedge maintain karna.

beats.onScreenIntent: Card 3: Pure alpha isolation across bull or bear markets

scenes.title: Stack & Roll vs Strip Hedge Mechanics
scenes.purpose: Comparative matrix of Stack-and-Roll versus Strip Hedging for long-dated exposures
takeaways: Long-dated exposures face illiquid distant futures
Stack and roll uses liquid front-month contracts
Contango produces cash drains and margin calls

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Commercial enterprises frequently sign fixed-price supply agreements with customers spanning five to ten years into the future. However, liquid exchange-traded futures contracts rarely trade with substantial volume beyond a few months or a year.

hi.display: Aksar ek enterprise ke paas five ya ten years ke long-term commercial commitments hote hain. Lekin futures contracts exchange par sirf six months tak hi heavily liquid hote hain.

beats.onScreenIntent: Stack and roll strategy row highlighted

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: To bridge this immense maturity mismatch, corporations implement a strategy known as Stack and Roll: the firm concentrates, or 'stacks', a massive volume of short-dated front-month futures contracts to match the total long-term physical commitment.

hi.display: Is maturity gap ko bridge karne ke liye companies Stack and Roll strategy use karti hain. Total long-term exposure ke barabar short-dated liquid futures contracts khareede jate hain, jise Stacking kehte hain.

beats.onScreenIntent: Strip hedge strategy row highlighted

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: The fatal flaw of stack and roll is rollover basis risk. Contango means distant futures trade above spot, while backwardation means spot trades above distant futures. In contango, rolling contracts generates persistent cash losses and margin calls.

hi.display: Stack and roll ki sabse badi weakness rollover basis risk hoti hai. Contango यानी distant futures spot se mehnga hona, jabki backwardation यानी spot distant futures se mehnga hota hai. Contango mein roll karne par cash drain aur margin calls face karni padti hain.

beats.onScreenIntent: Comparative summary matrix: liquidity versus rollover risk

cells: Buy contracts across all delivery months
Locked basis with zero cash drain
Severe rollover cash drain in contango

scenes.title: Case Study: The 1993 Metallgesellschaft Collapse
scenes.purpose: Historical post-mortem of how stack-and-roll triggered liquidity insolvency
takeaways: MGRM committed to 160M barrels of 10-year fuel supply
Long customer contracts hedged with short-term futures
Oil price collapse led to $1.33B net cash loss

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Consider Business Snapshot 3.2: the 1993 collapse of German conglomerate Metallgesellschaft. Its American subsidiary, MGRM, Metallgesellschaft Refining and Marketing, sold ten-year fixed-price heating oil and gasoline supply contracts covering 160 million barrels.

hi.display: Business Snapshot 3.2 mein German conglomerate Metallgesellschaft ka 1993 collapse dekhiye. Unki US subsidiary, MGRM, Metallgesellschaft Refining and Marketing ne customers ko ten-year fixed price par 160 million barrels oil supply karne ke contracts beche.

beats.onScreenIntent: Metallgesellschaft initial setup: 160M barrels guaranteed

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: To hedge this colossal exposure, MGRM stacked fifty-five million barrels of front-month NYMEX crude oil, heating oil, and gasoline futures, planning to roll the contracts forward month after month. On paper, the long-term physical sales and short-term futures hedges appeared balanced.

hi.display: Is exposure ko hedge karne ke liye MGRM ne NYMEX par massive short-dated futures buy karke unhe stack-and-roll karna shuru kiya. Paper par ye hedge perfectly balanced dikh raha tha.

beats.onScreenIntent: The maturity mismatch: 10-year contracts hedged with 1-month futures

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: However, in late 1993, global oil prices experienced a catastrophic collapse. Because futures contracts settle daily through marking to market, the NYMEX clearinghouse issued hundreds of millions of dollars in immediate cash margin calls against MGRM's stacked long positions.

hi.display: Lekin late nineteen ninety-three mein crude oil prices unexpectedly collapse ho gaye. NYMEX clearing house ne daily marking-to-market par hundreds of millions of dollars ka cash variation margin demand kiya.

beats.onScreenIntent: Market shifts into contango; rollover losses trigger catastrophic margin calls

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Here was the fatal vulnerability: Cash Flow Timing Mismatch. MGRM's physical customers paid their revenues gradually over ten years, but NYMEX required hundreds of millions in hard cash immediately! Facing severe liquidity exhaustion, parent company banks panicked, fired management, and forcibly liquidated all futures contracts into a depressed market, crystallizing an astronomical one-point-three-three billion dollar net cash loss.

hi.display: Problem ye thi ki customers se revenue agle ten years mein cash aana tha, lekin futures losses aaj cash mein pay karne the. Is Cash Flow Timing Mismatch ne MGRM par one point three three billion dollars ka cash drain create kiya, aur supervisory board ne panic hokar bottom par sabhi positions liquidate kar di.

beats.onScreenIntent: The $1.33B final liquidation: lesson on cash flow timing versus accounting hedge

scenes.title: Knowledge Check: Calculating Hedge Ratio
scenes.purpose: Check student mastery of minimum variance hedge ratio calculation
takeaways: Active recall: calculating optimal hedge ratio
Formula: 0.80 times 0.040 over 0.050 equals 0.64
Optimal hedge position neutralizes 64% of variance

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Let us test your understanding with an active recall calculation. Spot price standard deviation is zero point zero four zero. Futures standard deviation is zero point zero five zero. Their correlation rho is zero point eight zero.

hi.display: Aaiye active recall calculation se aapka understanding test karte hain. Spot price standard deviation sigma S zero point zero four zero hai. Futures standard deviation sigma F zero point zero five zero hai. Dono ke beech correlation rho zero point eight zero hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Quiz question presented with sigma_S = 0.04, sigma_F = 0.05, rho = 0.80

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Pause the video and calculate carefully... Recall the formula h star equals rho multiplied by sigma S divided by sigma F. What is the resulting optimal ratio?

hi.display: Formula apply kijiye aur chaar options ko closely evaluate kijiye. Pause and consider.

beats.onScreenIntent: Thinking interval and formula reminder

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: The correct answer is Option B: zero point six four. Multiply zero point eight zero by zero point zero four zero, then divide by zero point zero five zero. This yields zero point six four, hedging sixty-four percent of exposure.

hi.display: Sahi answer Option B hai: zero point six four. Formula lagaiye: zero point eight zero guna zero point zero four zero divided by zero point zero five zero. Result zero point six four aata hai, jo sixty-four percent optimal hedge ratio hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Reveal Option B (0.64) with complete mathematical walkthrough

data.question: A company cross-hedges an asset with spot volatility sigma S = 0.040 using futures with volatility sigma F = 0.050 and correlation rho = 0.80. What is the optimal hedge ratio?
data.explanation: Hedge ratio equals rho times spot volatility over futures volatility, giving 0.80 times 0.040 over 0.050 which equals 0.64.

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Synthesizing both parts of Chapter 3 delivers an indispensable truth for every risk professional: hedging is never merely about calculating theoretical basis spreads; it is fundamentally about actively managing cash flow liquidity.

hi.display: Chapter Three ke dono parts ko unite karne par hume ek profound corporate risk management lesson milta hai: Hedging sirf theoretical spread calculate karne ka naam nahi hai; hedging cash liquidity manage karne ka naam hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Core pedagogical synthesis: managing basis risk versus liquidity risk

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Without dedicated, committed credit lines capable of withstanding severe marking-to-market margin calls, even a mathematically perfect hedge can force a solvent corporation into bankruptcy, exactly as witnessed in the Metallgesellschaft disaster.

hi.display: Agar aapki company ke paas marking-to-market margin calls jhelne ke liye committed credit lines nahi hain, toh mathematically correct hedge bhi aapko bankruptcy ke kagaar par khada kar sakta hai, jaisa Metallgesellschaft ke sath hua.

scenes.title: Summary: The Eight Quantitative Hedging Rules
scenes.purpose: Institutional rules codifying cross hedging, beta adjustments, and roll risk
takeaways: Rules 1 & 2: Minimum variance ratio and contract sizing
Rules 3 & 4: Tailing margin interest and index beta
Rules 5 to 8: Beta steering, alpha, stack, and contango

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Let us codify the eight quantitative rules of cross hedging and portfolio risk management that govern institutional practice.

hi.display: Aaiye cross hedging aur portfolio risk management ke eight quantitative rules ko systematically summarize karte hain.

beats.onScreenIntent: Overview of the 8 quantitative hedging rules

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Rule 1 optimizes cross hedge sizing using the minimum variance hedge ratio formula. Rule 2 calculates optimal futures contracts by scaling the hedge ratio by relative exposure sizes.

hi.display: Rule 1 minimum variance hedge ratio se optimal cross hedge sizing karta hai. Rule 2 relative position sizes ko scale karke total contracts calculate karta hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Rules 1 and 2 highlighted: Cross hedge definition & h* formula

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Rule 3 dictates that tailing the hedge adjusts contract counts for daily interest on margin cash flows. Rule 4 uses stock index futures to immunize equity portfolios against systematic market risk.

hi.display: Rule 3 daily margin interest ke liye contract count ko tailing adjustment deta hai. Rule 4 stock index futures se equity portfolio ke systematic market risk ko immunize karta hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Rules 3 and 4 highlighted: Contract count N* & R2 effectiveness

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Rule 5 dynamically adjusts portfolio market beta using the beta differential formula. Rule 6 enables alpha isolation by removing index movements to isolate stock picking gains.

hi.display: Rule 5 beta differential formula se portfolio beta ko dynamically steer karta hai. Rule 6 market index moves ko eliminate karke pure stock selection alpha isolate karta hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Rules 5 and 6 highlighted: Tailing adjustment & beta hedging

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Rule 7 utilizes stack and roll strategies to hedge multi-year exposures with liquid front-month contracts. Rule 8 warns that contango markets turn stack and roll into catastrophic margin call drains.

hi.display: Rule 7 liquid front-month contracts ko stack and roll karke long-dated commitments hedge karta hai. Rule 8 warn karta hai ki contango markets mein rollover massive cash margin deficits create karta hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Rules 7 and 8 highlighted: Tactical beta shift & stack and roll discipline

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Master these eight rules to navigate real-world cross hedging with complete institutional discipline. You are now prepared for Chapter 4.

data.title: The Eight Quantitative Rules of Cross Hedging

rules.title: Rule 1: Minimum Variance Ratio
rules.text: Optimize cross hedge sizing using the minimum variance hedge ratio formula h-star equals rho times sigma S over sigma F.

rules.title: Rule 2: Contract Sizing
rules.text: Calculate required futures contracts N-star equals h-star times QA over QF by scaling relative exposure sizes.

rules.title: Rule 3: Tailing the Hedge
rules.text: Tail the hedge using total dollar values N-star equals h-star times VA over VF to neutralize daily margin interest.

rules.title: Rule 4: Stock Index Immunization
rules.text: Immunize equity portfolios against market crashes by shorting stock index futures N-star equals beta times VA over VF.

rules.title: Rule 5: Tactical Beta Steering
rules.text: Steer portfolio sensitivity dynamically using the beta differential formula N-star equals beta minus target beta times P over A.

rules.title: Rule 6: Alpha Isolation
rules.text: Isolate alpha and monetize superior stock selection by stripping broad index market swings with short futures.

rules.title: Rule 7: Stack and Roll
rules.text: Deploy stack and roll strategies to hedge multi-year commitments with liquid front-month contracts.

rules.title: Rule 8: Contango Rollover Risk
rules.text: Recognize that contango turns stack and roll into catastrophic cash drains and fatal margin calls.
